WORK.name: Northbridge HQ — the hybrid office day
WORK.client: Northbridge Financial (fictional global bank, regional HQ, 3,800 badge holders)
WORK.challenge: Attendance has settled at 2.4 days a week. Leaders want the office to be 'worth the commute' without adding cost.
WORK.users: Hybrid employees, team leads, visitors, front-of-house and restaurant staff.
WORK.constraints: Real-estate budget frozen; restaurant contract renewal in 16 months; union consultation for any change to service hours.
evidence: Badge data: Tuesday-Thursday peaks at 78% of desks, Monday and Friday below 30% [fictional]
Restaurant queue observed at 12:20-12:45: median wait 11 min [fictional observation]
Interview P07: 'I come in to see my team, then spend half the day on calls I could take at home.' [fictional quote]
Service desk: 34% of tickets are room booking or 'cannot find a quiet space' [fictional]
WORK.persona: Maya, the 'anchor-day coordinator' — team lead who books the room, orders lunch and loses 40 minutes a week organising her team's office day.
insights: People come for each other, not for the desk
Lunch is the main social anchor but the queue breaks the team moment
Quiet space is the missing ingredient on peak days
hmw: How might we make the team lunch a 20-minute moment instead of a 45-minute logistics task?
How might we help a team lead plan an anchor day in two minutes?
WORK.workshop_inputs: Persona Maya, current journey, 4 evidence cards, 3 HMW questions, 6 inspiration sheets.
ideas: Anchor-day planner in the existing workplace app
WORK.priorities: Now: team-table pre-booking (standard offer, adapted). Next: anchor-day planner (needs app capability check). Later: zoning pilot.
WORK.test: 2-week pilot on one floor, 6 teams; measures: queue time, team-lunch attendance, booking time, satisfaction pulse vs. baseline.
WORK.credentials: Microsoft (Future of Workplace & Community, 2026), Eli Lilly (The Cell, 2026), Santander (Campus Dining & Well-being, 2025), Colgate-Palmolive (Blue-collar co-creation, 2024) — listed in S06/S07; artifacts to verify in SharePoint.

PLAY.name: Riverside Arena — the matchday fan journey
PLAY.challenge: Fans miss the first minutes of the second half because of half-time queues; per-cap food spend is flat.
PLAY.users: Season-ticket holders, families, fans with access needs, kiosk staff, stewards.
PLAY.constraints: 15-minute half-time; fixed kiosk footprint; safety rules on crowd flow; seasonal staff with 1-day training.
evidence: Observation: 62% of kiosk transactions happen in a 9-minute window at half-time [fictional]
Accessible seating sections are 140 m from the nearest step-free kiosk [fictional site measure]
Fan survey: 'I give up on food if the queue is longer than the walk back' (verbatim theme, n=412) [fictional]
Staff interview S03: 'We pre-pour, but we run out of the popular items first.' [fictional quote]
PLAY.persona: Dev, the 'half-time sprinter' — season-ticket holder with two kids who wants food and the toilet in 15 minutes without missing kick-off.
insights: Half-time is a 15-minute logistics race, not a dining moment
Accessibility gaps concentrate at the same pinch point
Families decide before the match whether they will buy food
hmw: How might we let fans get food at half-time without missing the restart?
How might we make the step-free route the easiest route?
PLAY.workshop_inputs: Persona Dev, current matchday journey, half-time heat map, 3 HMW, 6 inspiration sheets.
ideas: Order-ahead to collection lockers by section
Family bundle pre-sold with the ticket
PLAY.priorities: Now: family bundle (adapted standard). Next: section lockers (capability check). Later: roaming sellers pilot.
PLAY.test: 3-match pilot in two stands; measures: half-time transactions, queue length, fans back in seat at restart, accessible-section feedback.
PLAY.credentials: Arsenal FC (Emirates Stadium Experience, 2025), Roland-Garros (F&B Experience, 2026), Edinburgh Zoo (Visitor Experience Redesign, 2024) — listed in S06/S07; artifacts to verify.

HEAL.name: St Aldric Hospital — the inpatient meal journey
HEAL.client: St Aldric Regional Hospital (fictional 600-bed acute hospital)
HEAL.challenge: Patient meal satisfaction is low and food waste on wards is high; families feel excluded from mealtimes.
HEAL.users: Inpatients (incl. dietary constraints), families, nurses, ward hosts, dietitians, kitchen team.
HEAL.constraints: Clinical diets and allergen rules; infection control; meal ordering 24 h ahead; nurse workload.
evidence: Ward audit: 31% of trays returned more than half full [fictional]
Ordering happens 24 h before; 1 in 5 patients changed ward or diet in between [fictional]
Interview F02 (daughter of patient): 'Nobody tells me when Dad has eaten.' [fictional quote]
Ward host shadowing: 18 min per round spent finding the right tray [fictional observation]
HEAL.persona: Ruth, the 'worried visitor' — daughter visiting her father after surgery, who wants to know he is eating and to help with choice.
insights: The 24-hour order breaks when the patient's situation changes
Families are an unused ally at mealtimes
Waste is a signal of choice failure, not only appetite
hmw: How might we let patients choose closer to the meal without breaking clinical safety?
How might we involve families in mealtimes without adding nurse workload?
HEAL.workshop_inputs: Persona Ruth (+ patient persona Arthur), current meal journey, 4 evidence cards, 3 HMW, 6 inspiration sheets.
ideas: Same-day bedside ordering with diet check
HEAL.priorities: Now: protected mealtimes (process change). Next: same-day ordering (capability + clinical validation). Later: family updates (privacy review).
HEAL.test: 4-week ward pilot; measures: plate waste, meal satisfaction, missed meals, host time per round, incident log (safety).
HEAL.credentials: Clariane (Repensons — care-home food XP, 2025, care homes not acute hospitals: transfer limits apply). Cincinnati Children's / Cooper materials exist on the V1 board (RACI, SOW, pre-read) — use only after confirming sharing rules.

LEARN.name: Lakeshore State University — the student campus day
LEARN.client: Lakeshore State University (fictional, 24,000 students) — FICTIONAL until a verified education credential is supplied
LEARN.challenge: Students leave campus after classes; dining participation is falling and students report food is unaffordable.
LEARN.users: Commuter students, residents, international students, students with dietary or financial constraints, library and dining staff.
LEARN.constraints: Meal-plan pricing set annually; diverse dietary and cultural needs; spaces owned by different departments.
evidence: Meal-plan uptake down 9 points in 2 years [fictional]
Timetable analysis: 40% of students have a gap of 2+ hours between classes [fictional]
Interview St11: 'I eat in my car because the library doesn't allow food and the cafeteria is full.' [fictional quote]
Survey: 'affordable' is the top driver, ahead of 'healthy' [fictional]
LEARN.persona: Leila, the 'between-classes commuter' — part-time worker on a tight budget who needs a place to eat, study and recharge for 3 hours.
insights: The real need is a 'home base' for the gap, not a meal
Affordability is about predictability as much as price
Food rules in study spaces push students out
hmw: How might we make the 3-hour gap the best part of a commuter's day?
How might we make eating on campus predictable for a tight budget?
LEARN.workshop_inputs: Persona Leila, current campus-day journey, 4 evidence cards, 3 HMW, 6 inspiration sheets.
ideas: Eat-and-study zones in the library annex
LEARN.priorities: Now: commuter bundle (adapted standard). Next: eat-and-study zone (space owner approval). Later: club partnerships.
LEARN.test: One-semester pilot; measures: bundle uptake, dwell time, zone occupancy, affordability perception survey vs. baseline.
LEARN.credentials: No education credential verified in the supplied decks (S05 lists a BRM for Education & Government; Cyber Campus is an innovation hub). Use as fictional case.
